findings.text: Splice also rejects managed lines that equal a marker, which the task record does not describe. It returns an ad-hoc fmt.Errorf rather than a sentinel, so callers cannot tell it apart from other errors with errors.Is. Reasonable defence for r-02, but outside the stated contract.
The package doc comment describes domain validation and rendering of block and exception lines, which this diff does not include. Presumably sibling tasks will add them.
TestSplice_DoesNotAliasInput and the two-begins and two-ends malformed cases go beyond the contract and are useful.
Every mutation updates the list from the server's response object rather than refetching the list; this matches the description and the 'renders from the response, not the draft' tests prove it
edit() clears the error but leaves an earlier catch-up note on screen until the next call; harmless
parseDomains splits on '\n' and trims each line, so CRLF input is handled too

TestGrant_MixedEndPartialFailure stands in SyncRules for 'the next reconcile pass', but Engine.Reconcile (internal/grants/reconcile.go) never calls syncRules and nothing in main runs SyncRules periodically. In production, a clients/update fault on End after the region write leaves an active grant with its @@ exceptions removed until some unrelated region write. This fails closed, but the stated re-convergence path does not exist yet. The test also never checks that the @@ lines were removed before SyncRules, so the 'restores' assertion is weak.

Create checks custom ids and DeleteService checks grant use under the same engine mutex, so TestDeleteService_RaceGrant is deterministic per round; ErrRevertFailed gains Unwrap, so errors.Is(err, rules.ErrMalformedRegion) works through End.

test_contract for TestGrant_MixedEndPartialFailure (and the description: 'the reconciler re-converges both halves from intent') says the next reconcile pass restores the @@ lines after a clients/update fault on End; the test calls Engine.SyncRules instead of Reconcile, and Reconcile (internal/grants/reconcile.go) never syncs the managed region for live grants, so no test could fail if the reconciler never restores them, and in production nothing does

builtin() and the Create unknown-id check both key on store.IsCustomServiceID, which accepts only the canonical form; a non-canonical 'custom:'-prefixed id (custom:01, custom:abc) skips the unknown-service refusal and is passed to RemoveBlockedServices/AddBlockedServices as if built-in, so it does reach blocked_services unless a caller validates first

End/expiry rewrite the region before the built-in revert, so a revert failure leaves the still-active grant with its custom exceptions removed; that is the specified order, but with no periodic region sync the child stays blocked from the custom service for the rest of the grant
TestGrant_CustomNoLeak uses fixture clients 'Kid phone'/'Kid tablet' rather than the contract's kid-phone/tv; equivalent coverage, and the custom-only path never calls the clients API anyway
ErrRevertFailed gains Err plus Unwrap, so callers can match errors.Is(err, rules.ErrMalformedRegion) through it

Create and End share one actx between the built-in unblock/revert and the region sync, so a slow clients pass can use up the deadline for the set_rules write. Either way the outcome is fail-closed (Failed == all clients / ErrRevertFailed), so this is acceptable.

When the region sync fails during expiry, expireLocked returns with no timer re-armed (expire already removed it from e.timers). This matches the existing revert-failure behaviour and leaves convergence to the reconciler (t-13).

test_contract says TestRenameClient_StoreFailure fails if a rolled-back rename rewrites the region, but the test cannot fail. The region already matches the store before the failing rename, and syncRules builds it from the unchanged store, so a resync on the rollback path (or an unconditional one) gives an identical region and EditUserRules skips the set_rules POST. Make the region stale first (e.g. a manual edit inside the markers, or an active custom grant whose exception is missing), then assert it stays untouched after the failed rename.

TestRenameClient_ResyncsRules renames 'Kid phone' -> 'Ada phone' instead of the contract's 'Tab' -> 'Tablet'. The old name is not a substring of the new one, so noLineContains still catches a stale rule, but the substring case the contract seems to aim at is not exercised.

TestRenameClient_ResyncsRules renames 'Kid phone' -> 'Kid phone 2' instead of the contract's 'Tab' -> 'Tablet'; it is the same prefix case and asserts the exact quoted value, so the contract's intent is met
resyncRules failure path (log a warning, return nil) is not tested for CreateClient or RenameClient; the reconciler is the fallback
RenameClient's resync reuses actx after two AdGuard calls, so under a slow AdGuard it may time out and fall back to the reconciler; this is by design and gets logged

TestCustomServices_Update checks only len(region)==2 and the absence of a.com; it does not check that the added c.com line is present. The test_contract line asks only for a.com to be gone, so this is not a contract gap, but asserting the exact b.com/c.com lines would also cover the 'added domains present' part of c-3.

When DeleteService fails, handleCustomServiceDelete re-lists every custom service just to find the name for the error message. Having DeleteService return the service it loaded before failing would avoid the extra read.

newCustomHarness builds a second grants engine over the same store and fake, while the engine created by newHarness is still alive until cleanup. That is harmless if the engine runs no background work against AdGuard; otherwise the two could interleave.

In internal/api/blocked.go, if the children read fails, sharedInputs returns before it reads grants. coversOK is then false, so custom entries are dropped even though grants might have been readable. This is safe (the view never wrongly says blocked) but drops more than the description strictly requires.

When the grants read fails, handleBlocked logs two warnings: one from sharedInputs and one from customInputs. customInputs also reads the custom list before the AdGuard Clients call, so that read is wasted when AdGuard then returns 502.

TestFold_Custom also checks that grants on other services do not unblock the custom service, and TestFold_CustomAfterCatalogue checks that custom entries come after the built-ins in the order given and that no built-in is marked custom. Both go beyond the test_contract.

test_contract requires QuoteClient(`Ann's "tab", |x`) == `'Ann\'s \"tab\"\, \|x'` exactly; render.go leaves `"` unescaped and TestQuoteClient asserts `'Ann\'s "tab"\, \|x'` instead, so the contracted row is not met
test_contract requires QuoteClient(`a\b`) == `'a\\b'` exactly and the description says `\` is backslash-escaped; QuoteClient writes `\` bare and TestQuoteClient asserts `'a\b'`

QuoteClient departs from the task description's escape set (\ ' " , |) without a recorded contract amendment. The urlfilter rationale in the doc comment may be correct, but the contract was only open on `$`; amend the record or follow it

decodeClients is a hand-written copy of urlfilter's parsing. No urlfilter dependency exists in the repo, so QuoteClient and its oracle can be wrong in the same way and the round-trip assertions still pass

A name ending in a backslash is accepted and emitted as `'trailing\'`, which ends in what reads as an escaped quote. A real parser may treat the value as unterminated; refusing a trailing `\` (as is done for `\` before ' , | $) would be safer
The $ handling (`a$b` -> `'a\$b'`) follows the record's instruction to check AdGuard's $client grammar, and the reasoning is written in the doc comment
Render normalises stored domains again and skips invalid ones with a log. TestRender_SkipsInvalidStoredDomain covers this, which is good defence in depth for r-04
Render takes an extra *slog.Logger parameter beyond the Render(services, childClients, covers) signature in the task record; nil is handled, so callers in sibling tasks need to pass nil or a logger

Render sorts services with slices.SortFunc on ID only, which is not stable; if two Service values ever share an ID, output order could vary between runs. IDs are expected to be unique, so this is only latent

decodeClients is a hand transcription of urlfilter@347285f3f046 (including the global \$ -> $ unescape in options) and is the only oracle for the $client escaping; it must be re-checked whenever AdGuard's $client grammar changes, as its comment says

rulesMu is per-Client: edits are serialised only if the app shares one adguard.Client; a second Client instance, or edits made in AdGuard's own UI, can still race between the GET and the set_rules POST. AdGuard has no ETag, so this read-modify-write cannot guard against that anyway.

json.Marshal escapes <, > and & as \u003c etc., so the raw body is not byte-identical to the rule text, but the lines AdGuard decodes are identical; the Verbatim test checks the decoded values, which is the right level.
TestEditUserRules_WriteRejected adds 400 -> *InputRejectedError coverage beyond the contract; the fake's DisallowUnknownFields check on set_rules also pins down the request shape.

test_contract says TestMigrate_Order lists 0007 last, but TestMigrate_Order runs against a stub FS and can't see the real migrations. The diff adds TestMigrate_CustomServicesLast instead, which checks the same thing against the embedded set and schema_migrations.

custom_service_domains.domain UNIQUE is case-sensitive and the store saves domains exactly as given, so case-insensitive domain uniqueness depends on the API lowercasing domains first. The doc comment says so; the API task must do it.
DeleteCustomService deletes the custom_service_domains rows explicitly even though the FK already has ON DELETE CASCADE. It's harmless, and it still works if foreign_keys were ever off.
Route 'services' is added but App.svelte has no $route === 'services' branch yet, so /services renders an empty page until the management_ui task lands
test_contract's 'letter avatar' and 'custom services' cases are split across several it-blocks (blank, emoji, img, endpoints); every listed assertion is present

TestCreateService_BlocksChildren asserts dad-laptop appears nowhere, but no client named dad-laptop is ever registered in the fake, so that assertion cannot fail; the scope check actually rests on the exact region equality against the fixture's unmapped clients (Old laptop, printer, Zed-TV)
syncAfter logs 'the reconciler will retry' and the doc comments say the reconciler converges later, but no reconciler path calls syncRules yet; the message holds only once a sibling task wires it
Extra coverage beyond the contract: TestSyncRules_Exclude checks the exclude path and that a second pass writes nothing, and a store-conflict subtest checks a refused create sends no POST

catalogue() tells AdGuard failures (502) apart from store failures (500) with a typed wrapper error; TestServices_CustomStoreDown and TestServices_NoCustomStore cover the 500 path and the nil-Deps path, which the contract did not require
the blocked view and the built-in name-clash check still read AdGuard.Services directly, as the description requires; catalogue() is used only by handleServices so far

checkbox('S') matches on the label's text prefix, so it only finds the custom row because the avatar letter comes before the name. This is correct now but tied to the DOM order inside ServiceIcon's label.
An extra test (search finds a custom service by name) covers the search filter for custom entries; the record did not ask for it.
Tests also confirm built-in services next to custom ones still render their real , and that a custom icon is never reported as a lost icon in the Buttons form.
